transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I've been feeling constantly depressed and sad for a very long time now. It has been going on continuously for over two years—about two years and a month, to be exact. I just can't seem to shake this heavy, low mood.
During these past two years, have there been any periods of two months or longer where you felt completely back to your normal self, or has your mood remained consistently low the entire time?

No, I haven't had any breaks like that at all. My mood has been consistently low and depressed for the entire two years and one month. There haven't been any periods of two months or longer where I felt back to normal, as this sadness and emptiness have been completely continuous.
Beyond feeling sad or low, have you experienced other symptoms like significant changes in your sleep, appetite, energy levels, or ability to concentrate during this time?
I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my sleep or appetite. My energy levels and concentration have also stayed pretty much the same.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports a continuous low mood for over two years without any two-month period of remission, and explicitly denies the classic vegetative symptoms (sleep, appetite, energy, concentration changes) required to meet the full criteria for a Major Depressive Episode. Therefore, Persistent Depressive Disorder is the primary candidate, and Major Depressive Disorder is removed.
